text:
sam: quick follow-up after the canary yesterday — we still see a tail-latency regression when routing to fa3+flashattn-v3 under medium burst load. numbers below. anyone else reproducing?

nora: saw it locally on a 3090 repro too. not huge P50 change but 95/99 moved. looks like backpressure from batching.

peter: can you paste the perf run you used? we should rule out workspace fragmentation first.

sam: pasted the microbench here:
```
./rt_bench --model vicuna-13b --kernel flashattn_v3 --batch_dist poisson --qps 120 --seq 1024 --warm 50 --iter 500
```

sam: results: P50 18ms, P95 62ms, P99 180ms. fallback kernel (flashattn_v2) under same load: P50 20ms, P95 45ms, P99 95ms. so v3 better at P50 but much worse at P99 in this config.

jin: interesting. do you have allocator and coalesce settings? v3 is more aggressive with workspace reuse and prefetch, could amplify stall on tail.

sam: default allocator + coalesce window 4ms. we tried coalesce=1ms and P99 dropped to ~120ms, still >v2.

nora: we also saw long contiguous allocation spikes when sequence length varies (interleaved short/long), might be fragmentation starving later requests until GPU defrag completes.

peter: theory: v3 kernel has a longer critical section holding the global workspace lock for large-seq kernels, so when batching bursts produce a long request, other small requests queue up and get delayed. need telemetry on hold times.

jin: agree. I can add a hook to kernel selection telemetry to log: kernel_name, seq_len, batch_size, workspace_claim_ms. will push a small change to canary.

infra-bot: canary deployment queued for cluster-2, image: runtime-flashopt:staging-2026-03-20-01

sam: thanks. also observed that enabling kv-cache changes the shape of batches (more multi-pass tokens) and worsens tail for v3. might be interaction with reuse policy.

nora: if kernel holds workspace across kv-cache repeats that could starve new kernels. maybe change workspace_claim to be ref-counted per-request rather than global hold?

peter: or implement preemptible workspace: allow high-priority small requests to steal after X ms. complexity high but might be fast win for P99.

jin: I'll instrument first before design. logs will emit every time workspace claim >5ms with stack id and seq_len, then we can correlate with request types.

sam: for experiments let's run two A/B configs on canary: A) coalesce=1ms + conservative workspace timeout 30ms, B) coalesce=4ms + preemptible prototype (steal after 20ms). compare P99 and throughput.

nora: also add a synthetic workload with interleaved seqs: [64,64,1024,64,256,64] to maximize fragmentation signal.

peter: one more data point: on an A100 we saw smaller P99 delta between v3 and v2. might be hardware sensitivity (SM schedulers, memcpy overlap). include both 3090 and A100 in tests.

jin: added telemetry PR: https://git.redwood/re/runtime/pulls/432 - will post logs to #eng-runtime.

sam: perfect. assign follow-ups: jin = telemetry + canary, nora = synthetic workload harness, peter = workspace preemptible proposal writeup (short doc), me = run A/B and collect numbers.

nora: acked. will run harness across gpu types and post csv.

peter: will sketch proposal in /doc and ping for review tomorrow.

sam: thanks all. hoping to have numbers by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
